extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers, PIs, and institutional research administrators interested in NIGMS funding
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and interpreting NIGMS investigator- and program-level funding metrics (award counts, award rates, award sizes, program eligibility) to inform investigators and institutions about trends and policy effects such as MIRA. Includes methodological notes on how comparisons and reporting are done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of PIs holding more than one NIGMS R01
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure 1 shows the percentage of PIs who held more than one NIGMS R01 between fiscal years 2014 and 2024 (FY14 and FY24). In FY14 and FY15, only 16% of PIs had more than one NIGMS R01. This percentage hovered around 14-15% until 2019, when it began declining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess how common multiple R01 holdings are and to evaluate effects of program changes (e.g., conversions to MIRA and institute policies). The decline was likely due to increasing conversions of R01s to MIRAs and an Institute policy limiting PIs to no more than two NIGMS R01s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute policy: limit on number of NIGMS R01s per PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute policy that PIs could not have more than two NIGMS R01s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy affects distribution of R01 holdings and interpretation of multi-R01 statistics (explains part of observed declines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative investigator rate
rubrics_metrics.description: At NIGMS, we focus on supporting a broad group of investigators. As a result, we monitor two statistics that describe our investigator pool: the cumulative investigator rate and the number of funded early stage investigators (ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A monitored statistic to describe the composition of the investigator pool over time; used alongside ESI counts to assess portfolio diversity and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of funded Early Stage Investigators (ESIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure 1 illustrates the number of ESIs who received their first competing NIGMS R01-equivalent grants each year between FY2013 and FY2022. In FY2022, NIGMS awarded R01-equivalent grants to 319 ESIs in total: 31 investigators received R01 awards, 268 investigators received R35 (MIRA) awards, and 20 investigators received NIH Director’s New Innovator Awards (DP2s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track year-to-year counts of newly funded ESIs to evaluate support for early-career investigators; note that program composition (e.g., MIRA introduction) affects trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of DP2s administered by NIGMS in ESI counts
rubrics_metrics.description: These data include DP2s (four awards) administered by NIGMS on behalf of the NIH Office of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which award mechanisms are counted as R01-equivalent for ESI statistics; important for reproducibility and comparability of counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award rates (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award rates: the percentage of reviewed applications that receive funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare programs (e.g., MIRA renewals vs R01 renewals) and cohorts (EIs vs ESIs). When reporting award rates, specify denominator (reviewed applications) and subgroup definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award counts and award rates by fiscal year and investigator type
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 shows the number of new awards made and associated award rates by fiscal year for Established Investigators (EIs) and Early Stage Investigators (ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate counts and rates by investigator status (EI vs ESI) and fiscal year to reveal differential outcomes and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award sizes and budget reporting (yearly direct costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: We compare award sizes for MIRA renewals and R01 renewals and examine award size changes for FY2021 renewals. All budget values shown in the post are yearly direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing award sizes, use yearly direct costs as the unit and, where possible, distinguish between investigator groups (EIs, ESIs, ex-ESIs) because they often have different characteristics for award sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish renewals and conversions (MIRA renewals, R01 renewals, R01→MIRA conversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS funded its first round of renewals for the MIRA program in FY2021. The post compares award rates and award sizes of MIRA renewals and R01 renewals and examines award rates and budget changes for investigators applying to convert their NIGMS R01s to MIRAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate analyses for renewals and for conversions help illuminate program-specific outcomes; report sample sizes and subgroup distinctions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA program research-effort and NIGMS-eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA provides investigators with flexibility and stability for their research programs. Investigators who receive MIRA support must dedicate 51% of their research effort toward the grant and are ineligible to apply for or receive other NIGMS research support (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This eligibility/effort requirement is a constraint that affects grantee behavior (e.g., ability to hold other NIGMS awards) and should be accounted for in analyses of application behavior and post-award activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative-methods standard: matched comparator groups for comparing MIRA vs R01 behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare application behavior between MIRA and R01-funded investigators, we created sets of both established (EI) and early stage (ESI) investigators supported by NIGMS R01s who have not received a MIRA. The EI comparators were matched according to race/ethnicity, gender, time since acquisition of first R01, and average annual NIGMS funding. For the ESI comparator group, we used all ESI NIGMS R01 awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing cohorts, match on demographics and funding history variables to reduce confounding; be explicit about matching variables and comparator selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting privacy rules for small groups and limitations on intersectional analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to privacy requirements and small numbers, applicants from underrepresented racial and ethnic groups in biomedical research (Black or African American, Hispanic or Latino, American Indian or Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian and other Pacific Islander) are combined into a larger group that can be reported. Because of the small applicant numbers, we’re unable to show intersectional analyses of race/ethnicity and gender or analyses of applicants with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate small subgroups to preserve confidentiality; explicitly state when intersectional analyses cannot be reported because of small sample sizes and privacy constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: AREA (R15) program eligibility and award parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: AREA grants support small-scale research projects involving primarily undergraduate students at institutions that received no more than $6 million in funding from NIH in 4 of the past 7 years. Awards can be up to $300,000 in direct costs for the entire project period of up to 3 years. R15 funds are obligated in the first year and last the duration of the project period. Grantees can renew these awards in a competitive proposal process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional NIH funding history to determine eligibility; note distinctive funding structure (funds obligated in year 1 for the full project period) and renewal modality (competitive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between AREA and REAP
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH offers two different R15 awards: AREA and the Research Enhancement Award Program (REAP). The key distinction between them is that AREA grants are available to undergraduate-focused institutions, while REAP grants are available to health professional and graduate schools. NIGMS participates in only the AREA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct R15 mechanism based on institution type and be explicit about which programs an institute participates in when reporting portfolio data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio transparency: monitor and publish investigator- and program-level annual trends
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of its commitment to transparency, NIGMS examines and publishes data on annual trends reflected in its RPG portfolio. Posts review and describe investigator-level trends associated with competing R01/R01-equivalent RPGs including those in the Institute’s R35 MIRA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular, public reporting of annual trends (applications, awards, rates, demographics) supports transparency and stewardship; ensure clarity on which mechanisms and cohorts are included in analyses.
